newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-THREE MORE SEEDS MAKE EARLY EXITS IN AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-THREE MORE SEEDS MAKE EARLY EXITS IN AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Australia's Mark Woodforde led another exodus of seeded players out of the Australian Hardcourt tennis championship at Memorial Drive on Thursday.
Second seed Woodforde was beaten 6-3 6-4 by Karol Kucera of Slovakia in their second-round match while sixth seed David Prinosil of Germany fell 6-2 6-4 to fiery American qualifier Jeff Tarango.
Eighth seed Bohdan Ulihrach of the Czech Republic continued the trend when he was beaten 7-6 1-6 6-3 by Australian wildcard entrant Scott Draper in an evening match.
Woodforde, who won the title in 1988 and 1989, was unable to counter Kucera's unpredictable service game despite the support of his home crowd.
"He takes the ball early and his serve is pretty deceiving," Woodforde told reporters.
"It's pretty ugly and it doesn't look like it's coming over the net. I certainly had trouble with it," he said.
Draper will meet Kucera in the quarter-finals.
Tarango's quarter-final opponent will be Jonas Bjorkman after the unseeded Swede beat Jonathan Stark of the United States 6-4 6-2.
Australia's Todd Woodbridge and Alex O'Brien of the United States, seeded fourth and fifth respectively, were the only seeded players to make it through to the quarter-finals.
Top-seeded Russian Yevgeny Kafelnikov, third seed Andrei Medvedev of the Ukraine and seventh seed Renzo Furlan of Italy were all beaten in the first round.
